chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Suleyman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:
A man (peace be upon him) wrote to me: In the prostration of gratitude, say one hundred times: 'Thanks, thanks', and if you wish, 'Pardon, pardon'.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for Sajdat al-Shukr (prostration of gratitude) in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the specific dhikr of 'Shukran' (Thanks) or 'Afwan' (Pardon) recited one hundred times during the prostration of gratitude (Sajdat al-Shukr), a practice emphasized by Shia scholars as a means to deepen spiritual connection after prayer. The choice between 'Shukran' and 'Afwan' reflects the dual nature of divine favor, acknowledging both blessings and mercy. This act serves as a practical expression of thankfulness, reinforcing the believer's awareness of God's continuous grace.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya and Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhamad Bin Ahmad, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Suleyman Bin Hafs Al Marouzy who said,
‘A manasws wrote to me: ‘In the Sajdah-e-Shukr (prostration of gratefulness), (say) one hundred times, ‘Thanks! Thanks!’, and if you so desire to, ‘Pardon! Pardon!’.
en.sarwar: 20. Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris have narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasaniy from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwaziy who has said the following:
“The man, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, wrote to me the following: ’During sajdah when expressing thanks to Allah say, “Shukran” one hundred times - or if you wanted - say “’Afwan ‘Afwan.’””
